Linux disks are a separate exec because a large combined request is rejected by Dropbear; the awk parser excludes network and FUSE capacity and counts a shared APFS capacity once. macOS keeps its sysctl/vm_stat/ps/netstat command and direct CPU percentage. GPU is best-effort through nvidia-smi and is absent rather than an error when the command is unavailable. Deliberate divergence: the GPU query runs inside the same metric exec on every sample, where the original cached a separate probe for 10-30 seconds; the two-second nvidia-smi timeout bounds the cost and every metric shares one round trip. An unknown OS is a typed unsupported state. A metric the reply does not carry is NaN (a dash), while a reply with no recognizable metric is a typed unsupported failure. Sampling runs in service goroutines through the connection layer's channel lease, never a terminal Session. |

The original wrote a local temp archive, uploaded it, then ran a staged extract with backup and rollback; this stream packs tar.gz into the remote tar over the same connection's exec channel, extracts into a sibling .netcatty-extract-* directory, and promotes each target by rename. Every extracted entry is read back before promotion: a directory must be a directory and a file's size must equal the plan (ADR-0012). Any preflight refusal, unsafe name, symlink, special file, move, conflict, resume row, extraction failure, short extraction, or cancellation never publishes partial data; a failed extraction is removed and the ordinary per-file copy runs instead. The packer reads one byte past each planned size so a source that grew is refused instead of publishing a prefix. An exec transport that cannot half-close is refused before any byte is written rather than risking a killed tar. |

A deterministic dirs-first sorted plan yields totals, identities, and copy order. A resumed Transfer re-walks the tree, requires completed == covered, and skips the verified prefix. Paused and failed rows freeze progress to the checkpoint prefix, the chosen destination roots are pinned in Targets, and a restart keeps both across DowngradeInterrupted. Each row persists the saved Host behind its endpoints (`sourceHost`/`destHost`), so reconnecting a Host in the SFTP pane reaches Queue.ReattachHost and binds that Host's fresh filesystem to every matching interrupted row, including a row whose transport was lost, while an ordinary failure and a finished row keep their state; Resume then continues from the checkpoint and Retry remains a full replay. Rows persisted before the endpoint fields existed infer their direction from the request-ordered queue lanes, so a legacy upload's Host is its destination and a download's Host is its source. A row whose Host is still disconnected keeps the reconnect prompt and refuses Resume with ErrTaskUnavailable. A resumed queued Transfer stages each file under a name derived from its durable Task ID and target, so it reuses and promotes away the interrupted process's `.part` instead of leaving an orphan, while another task's staging file is untouched. |

Only then does rename take the destination name. The original is renamed to its stable sibling backup before the first staged file is promoted, so an ordinary failure removes the partial tree and renames the backup back; a pause or a lost transport keeps the partial tree and backup for the resume instead, matching the ticket-32 contract. A backup left beside a live file destination is stale and removed, while a backup beside a missing destination is the only known-good copy and is restored before the new transaction starts; a backup beside an existing directory root is always restored over it, because an attempt that died before its checkpoint may have created an empty root. A committed replacement removes both artifacts; if the backup cannot be removed, the destination stays promoted, the backup stays recoverable, and the operation reports the cleanup failure. Unlike the original's whole-directory staged tree, this build keeps the accepted ticket-32 in-place tree replacement per file, so a folder replacement is transactionally covered by its backup and rollback rather than one directory rename. |

Inspect and logs load into a bounded read-only document: 64 KiB with a marker on truncation, and logs clamped to 1..1000 lines with 200 by default. Loading is cancellable off the UI thread, closing cancels it, and a reply that arrives after a newer request or a close is dropped. A missing Docker command, a stopped daemon, or a permission denial degrades only inside the Docker tab; the other tabs keep sampling. The default cadence is five seconds. Deliberate divergences: start and stop also pass through the shared confirmation, as this build's ticket requires, where the original confirmed only removal; container icons and an interactive container shell from the original are not reproduced, so logs and inspect are read-only documents and an interactive shell remains a terminal-surface concern. |

The application layer validates every record, compares its Host merge key (protocol, hostname, port, username, group) with the current Vault, and reports conflicts, in-file duplicates, and invalid source rows by row number before writing anything. The user selects rows and chooses Skip or Overwrite; there is no implicit overwrite. New Hosts and their missing ancestor Groups are saved in one SQLite transaction per 50-row chunk, and Next/Offset resumes a retried chunk without duplicate Hosts. Passwords, proxy passwords, and referenced IdentityFiles go through the field-secret store and Key inspector, so plaintext never enters a Host record or the database. Imported Hosts retain tags, notes, proxy settings, Key references, the SSH agent preference, and ProxyJump chains, and the preview exposes no credential material.
